trail.text: Flagged window shows catalogue and queue-master spiking — I'll drill in to separate cause from victim.
Catalogue is spiking hard while orders and front-end look flat — I'll scan the remaining services for other victims.
Catalogue's database is quiet, pointing to local file activity — I'll check the rest of the fleet for the next-strongest signals.
Everything else is nearly flat, leaving three clear outliers — now I'll pin down timing to identify the origin.
Early timing favors catalogue as the leader — I'll pull the time series to confirm the onset order.
The series confirms an abrupt step in catalogue with a gradual ramp elsewhere — I'll do a final sweep for any other deviating services before ranking.

causes.reasoning: Step from 0 to 2.2M at 1s, earliest change, with FS reads/writes 0->3162, cache 20k->2.2M, cpu-system 0.28->41.7 and p99 latency 0.009->0.073 while catalogue-db is flat, indicating local file/cache churn inside catalogue causing CPU and latency.
FS writes/reads 0.03->19.3 and bytes 523->81570 ramping from 11s after catalogue with no CPU or latency increase, indicating collateral host-level or downstream victim rather than origin.
Host disk writes 89->3533 from 3s after catalogue step with CPU/network flat, consistent with the host backing the catalogue container storm rather than an independent root cause.
Only mild memory rise 70.8M->73.9M score 4.18 with tiny FS/CPU moves, likely noise and far smaller and later than catalogue storm.
Only cache 0.7M->1.38M score 3.68 with no CPU/FS storm, likely background noise unrelated to the catalogue file/CPU spike.
